purpose: Adversarial benchmark contract for comparing Teleon pipeline-template authoring variants on a local business workflow before formalizing the recommended usage.

business_problem.summary: Normalize an invoice-like vendor task, validate required fields, score risk, and emit a candidate review packet.
business_problem.reason: The workflow is business-shaped, local, deterministic, side-effect-free, and representative of acquire-normalize-validate-score-emit pipelines.

usage_lanes.why: LLM emits only primitive ids or small slot bindings; deterministic compiler expands them.
Local Python authors can write one callable per line without step labels or primitive strings.
Authors can attach or override metadata explicitly when inference is not enough.
Lists, dicts, and matrices preserve grouping while still compiling to linear step specs.
A domain object can expose to_teleon_primitives without letting the compiler crawl arbitrary internals.
Verbose step specs are easiest to inspect after compilation, even if they are not the cheapest LLM output.

default_recommendation.law: There is no single universal winner. Recommendations are per usage lane and can change when a new variant beats the incumbent under the benchmark.
default_recommendation.reason: Every allowed authoring surface compiles into the same deterministic serializable step specs. The contract chooses incumbents by lane rather than pretending one surface is best for all use cases.

acceptance_laws: All allowed variants compile and execute successfully.
All allowed variants produce the same semantic business output.
Each allowed variant is deterministic across repeated runs.
compact_json_ids uses fewer planner payload tokens than verbose_json_steps.
At least six authoring variants are evaluated; the benchmark may not hard-code a binary choice.
Every usage-lane incumbent appears in the evaluated variant set.
The highest-flexibility variant is an explicit Python object-graph form, not a raw JSON surface.
Unsupported primitive ids, invalid state roots, arbitrary object crawling, and JSON import/code surfaces are rejected.
All benchmark reports and compiled outputs remain serves_truth=false.

contract_evolution.rule: A future authoring variant can become recommended only if this checker is extended with a named variant, the variant beats or ties the current recommendation on token proxy, determinism, and flexibility for at least one declared usage lane, and the full proof gate remains green.
contract_evolution.versioning: Changes to variant semantics require a new contract version and must preserve old lockfile execution semantics or provide an explicit migration.
